analysis.title: GS Consumer: 3 Key Themes
key_insights: Consumer bellwethers report over the next few days: AS, HD and VIK on Nov 17, with more on Wednesday and Thursday.
Goldman's prime brokerage (GS PB) data shows significant shorting in the Staples sector as it makes all-time highs.

XLP hit another all-time high on Nov 16. The group is +10% over the last month and +21% YTD. The note calls it largely one big market momentum trade, with better 3Q earnings in much of HPC and Beauty as a secondary driver.

Staples flows: buying when the group first rallied a month ago, then net selling for the last 2 weeks as investors shorted the strength. Last week GS PB saw 6-1 selling over buying in Staples, led almost entirely by shorts and spread across Staples sub-sectors. Feiler concludes investors are fighting the move, not embracing it.
The desk expects more earnings beats than misses in retail over the next 2 weeks, though not a perfect set of results.
Feiler views the AS and HD beats on Nov 17 as expected. Both also raised the sales guide.
The desk expects strong results from TGT, LOW, WMT, WSM, ROST and BJ. TJX is seen as the hardest client-sentiment hurdle this week because investor feedback says the quarter was choppy.
Into next week, expectations are for upside at BBY, KSS and ANF.
Discretionary was one of only 3 sub-sectors with net buying last week, and is one of the few sectors with net buying over the last 1.5 weeks.
November is historically the best month of the year for Retail. Most of the outperformance over the last 10 years came in the last 2 weeks of the month (Black Friday).
HD reported a beat and raised its sales guide to the top of the prior range, with LOW reporting Nov 18. Investors had expected small top-line upside and generally in-line EPS at both.

Home improvement data feedback has been stable through 3Q despite a very tough housing environment. HD and LOW have held up despite high-profile sell-side downgrades from other firms. Feiler asks whether the reason is expectations of the beat, optimism on housing policy relief (which he doubts), or positioning.

sector_views.rationale: GS PB data shows heavy shorting and net selling into all-time highs, with investors fighting the rally. The note makes no explicit rating call.
The desk expects more beats than misses in retail EPS over the next 2 weeks, strong November seasonality, and net buying in Discretionary.

earnings_insights: HD reported 3Q on 11/17 with a beat and raised its sales guide to the top of the prior range. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.
AS also reported on 11/17 with a beat and a raised sales guide. The note gives no figures.
The desk expects strong results (beats vs minimal misses) from TGT, LOW (reports 11/18), WMT, WSM, ROST and BJ. These are expectations, not reported results.
TJX is the biggest client-sentiment hurdle this week because investors say the quarter was choppy.
The desk expects upside at BBY, KSS and ANF in the week of Nov 23.
Investor feedback going into HD and LOW was for small top-line upside and generally in-line EPS.
risk_factors: Staples momentum could keep squeezing the shorts, since the group is making all-time highs while investors short it.
TJX 3Q results may disappoint given choppy-quarter feedback from investors.
The housing environment is very tough, and the cause of HD and LOW's resilience is unclear.
Sell-side downgrades of HD and LOW from other firms.
vol_and_positioning: GS PB data: Staples were 6-1 better for sale last week, led almost entirely by shorts, across Staples sub-sectors.
Staples flows turned from buying a month ago to net selling over the last 2 weeks as the group hit all-time highs.
Discretionary was one of only 3 sub-sectors bought last week, and one of the few sectors with net buying over the last 1.5 weeks.
cross_bank_references: HD and LOW have both held in very well, despite some very high profile sell-side downgrades (away from us)
